posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md:
> Hans, if you and other pulsed enthusiasts put it on the Wiki, it will be easier to find in the future for other holographers.

Sorry, I don't think I am knowledgeable enough yet to post about this on the Wiki John. I will like to start building a pulse laser as well. But I am afraid to order parts because I don't know yet what doping concentrations of the crystals I should order for. My main question is for example: What is the most used nd doping for nd:YLF and nd:YAG? And what doping should I order for nd:glass? Also, should I order crystals with the ends cut at Brewsters or just plane parallel?

So many questions. But if I choose wrongly I invest thousands of Euros in the wrong parts.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: There is a copy of the old Rotorwave site on Sam's FAQ I think. If not I have one somewhere. It had great information including the best spreadsheet for designing pulsed lasers for holography I have ever seen. I would stay away from glass till you have a resonator working. Since it is your first one, make a resonator and get it working. Then make a Nd:YAG amplifier and push it through a frequency doubling crystal. Then worry about getting 10 J or whatever you spec is.

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md: I would like to have a go at making a nd:YLF laser because it has a much longer fluorescence time. That should make pumping a little easier and help with efficiency. Also, nd:glass is more suited to use with nd:YLF than with nd:YAG. I still need to know what doping % I need to order, and perhaps more importantly, before I order anything I need to know if I can use the same types of KDP for the slightly shorter (11nm) wavelength of the nd:YLF. I would like to be able to use components that were meant for nd:YAG. But will the 11nm difference in wavelength prevent me from doing so?
